title: Research Radar
text: Each article is the unit of analysis. Its thematic profile is stored with the article itself, and the overall radar is calculated from those article-level profiles. Scores do not represent article quality, journal rank, or scientific impact; they describe the relative thematic emphasis of each study on a 0–10 scale.

Research profile









The aggregate profile is the arithmetic mean of the 13 article-level profiles. It summarizes the research portfolio without assigning a separate score to a thematic block.

title: Research Radar
text:
Interpretation
The portfolio is concentrated in surface hydrology, hydrometeorology, statistical hydrology, uncertainty analysis, and hydroinformatics. Water-resources applications are present as a secondary dimension, while river hydraulics is peripheral in the current set of studies.
Hydrogeology and water quality are absent from the represented articles. The radar therefore describes the actual thematic coverage of the portfolio rather than an intended or normative disciplinary profile.

title: Research Radar
text:
How to read the scores
The 0–10 values are article-level descriptors. A value close to 10 indicates that a domain is central to the study; intermediate values indicate a substantive but secondary role; values close to 0 indicate that the domain is peripheral or absent. The aggregate radar is calculated directly from these article-level values.

title: About
text:
I hold a B.Sc. in Mechanical Fluids Engineering and work in hydrology, hydraulics and water resources analysis.
My research focuses on hydrological modelling, precipitation analysis, uncertainty assessment and environmental data science. I am particularly interested in understanding how data limitations, modelling choices and methodological assumptions influence hydrological predictions and decision-making in data-scarce environments.
My current research explores rainfall–runoff modelling, satellite and gridded precipitation products, extreme event analysis, and the application of statistical and machine learning methods in hydrology.
This website serves as a repository of publications, research projects, technical notes and reproducible workflows developed using R, GIS tools and open hydrological datasets.

title: Technical Notes
text: This section contains technical notes, reproducible workflows and open-source tools related to hydrology, hydraulics and environmental data science.

title: Technical Notes
text:
Tools

Automated IDF Report Generator in R
An open-source workflow for automated frequency analysis of annual maximum precipitation series and generation of Intensity–Duration–Frequency (IDF) reports.
The toolkit includes an R script, an R Markdown template, example files and documentation required to generate station-based IDF reports automatically.

Features

Frequency analysis of annual maximum precipitation
Design rainfall estimation for multiple return periods
IDF curve generation
Automatic PDF report creation
Report output in Spanish



Download
Download IDF Toolkit (ZIP)



ANA Hydrometeorological Station Auditor
A reproducible workflow for auditing the national hydrometeorological station inventory of the Peruvian National Water Authority (ANA).
The tool is designed to explore hydrometric and pluviometric stations across Peruvian basins and evaluate the temporal availability and completeness of their observational records.

Features

Basin-by-basin exploration of ANA stations
Hydrometric and pluviometric station inventories
Identification of first and last available observations
Record completeness assessment
Evaluation of common observational periods
Detection of missing-data patterns and long data gaps
Support for screening stations for hydrological research

The project is intended to provide a transparent first-stage audit before downloading and processing large observational datasets.



FABDEM Catchment Delineator v1.2
A reproducible catchment delineation workflow based on the 30 m FABDEM digital elevation model.
The tool is designed to generate watershed boundaries from user-defined outlet locations while handling the underlying DEM coverage and preprocessing required for hydrological terrain analysis.

Features

Catchment delineation from outlet points
FABDEM 30 m terrain data
Automated DEM tile identification
Processing of multi-tile catchments
Hydrologically consistent terrain preprocessing
Support for Peruvian and transboundary basins
Reproducible GIS outputs for subsequent hydrological analysis
